  1. Show HN: Mastra Factory, the open-source software factory we use to build Mastra

    • AI
    • Open Source
    • Software Development

    145 points · 42 comments · 18 Nov 2026, 16:53 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — Mastra Factory is an open-source, configurable agentic kanban system for software work, operated through a web UI and Slack. Its self-post says Mastra uses durable agents, memory, a cited Markdown wiki, PR-comment signals, cloud sandboxes, and a coding harness; it reports 238 Factory-opened-and-merged PRs and 630 human PRs in one week, alongside hosted and self-hosted options.

    Discussion — Discussion centered on the maintainers' decision to close their main repository to outside contributors because of low-value automated PRs, while requesting high-quality issue reproductions. Readers asked how autonomy, plans, model/harness integration, agent identity, UX validation, and human approval work. The team said lower-risk work can be more automated and that sandbox preview environments support UI testing.

  2. Show HN: ExitPath – Open-source ways out of Slack, Notion and Microsoft 365

    • Open Source
    • Self-Hosting

    249 points · 93 comments · 18 Nov 2026, 16:04 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — ExitPath is a no-account, browser-local migration planner/catalog for leaving 19 proprietary tools, including Slack, Notion, Google Workspace, and Microsoft 365. It lists 41 open-source alternatives and 60 migration paths, adjusts effort grades by team size and hosting choice, and offers checklists; it explicitly says most catalog entries are unreviewed AI drafts.

    Discussion — Readers found the consolidated catalog useful but stressed that migration pain is operational as well as technical: calendaring, identity/SSO, integrations, usability, and self-hosting burden. Zulip received positive firsthand reports; commenters disputed or refined particular recommendations and requested broader project-management coverage.

  3. All AI-generated code should be Open Source

    • AI
    • Copyright
    • Open Source

    1285 points · 673 comments · 15 Nov 2026, 14:46 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — The essay argues that AI-generated code should be open source, citing training on publicly available material and uncertainty around copyrightability of purely AI-generated output. It distinguishes fully automated output from mixed human-and-AI authorship but favors open release for lightly reviewed or prompt-only code.

    Discussion — The dominant response was that public-domain status is not the same as open source: copyright is generally needed to impose open-source license conditions. Commenters also disputed whether AI-assisted code is necessarily uncopyrightable and whether the proposed rule is workable.

    Week of 2026-11-20
